subject: RE: EdgeSummit — finalizing booth placement & sightline request
messages:
From: Simon Kline <simon@edgesummit.io>
To: alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Booth placement options for Redwood — endcap preference?

Hi Alex,

Quick follow up from our site planning call — we have two remaining premium slots in Hall B for Redwood: an endcap (B12-EC) adjacent to the main aisle, and an inline corner (B26-I). The endcap gives stronger sightlines from the main corridor but has a slightly narrower loading window; the inline corner is wider but set back ~6ft from the main thoroughfare.

I've attached the latest floorplan (EdgeSummit_floorplan_v4.pdf) and a quick visibility rendering (booth-visibility-rendering.png). Could you confirm which slot you'd prefer and whether you need a dock-side escort (freight-window-instructions.docx) for crate unloading? We need final confirmation by 6/18 to lock graphics and AV runs.

Thanks,
Simon Kline
Head of Exhibitor Ops
EdgeSummit

--
Attachment(s): EdgeSummit_floorplan_v4.pdf (pdf), booth-visibility-rendering.png (png), freight-window-instructions.docx (docx)
From: alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
To: Simon Kline <simon@edgesummit.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Booth placement options for Redwood — endcap preference?

Simon —

Appreciate the options and the visuals. Quick internal check: our primary goals are walk-by visibility (to maximize demo impressions) and a short freight path for crate unloading — we can accept a slightly narrower footprint if sightlines are strong.

Marissa, can you confirm whether the endcap's narrower loading window will cause any issues for the demo counter crate we usually bring (48" x 36" x 42", two crates)? Also looping Lauren for any catering/lead-gen touchpoints that might change the preferred flow.

Tentative preference for endcap B12-EC pending loading confirmation. If that's untenable, we'll take the inline corner. Can you hold the endcap until 6/18 as requested?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Booth placement options for Redwood — endcap preference?

Alex / team —

Checked with our freight vendor and the show yard: the endcap B12-EC has a 6ft-wide freight window but a 12ft push distance from the dock to the booth footprint. That will be a little tighter for two crates side-by-side, but workable if we schedule a 30-minute dock slot with a dolly team. Recommended actions:

- Reserve a dedicated 09:00 dock slot on load-in day and request a freight escort (EdgeSummit offers one free escort per exhibitor).
- Order a dolly + two-person lift crew (vendor quote attached in the Drive link).
- For graphics, compress the backwall artwork 2in on each side to accommodate the slightly angled sightline — designer can update once slot is confirmed.

If we cannot secure the escort or the morning slot, switch to inline B26-I. For now I think endcap is the right call given the visibility lift.

Logan — flagging you for AV power runs near the endcap; show said AV conduit is available but needs advance routing.

Marissa Cole
Senior Events Manager
Redwood Inference

Simon —

Confirming we will take endcap B12-EC. Please hold for Redwood and reserve the 09:00 dock slot on load-in day and note we will need a freight escort. Attached: designer note for backwall artwork compression (I'll share the file to the Drive link) and crate dimensions below for the dock team.

Crates: 2 x (48" x 36" x 42") — will require dolly + 2-person lift. AV: please route conduit to the endcap base point labelled P3 on the attached floorplan.

Simon, can you confirm the dock slot reservation and whether EdgeSummit will assign the escort? Also confirm contact name/phone for on-site ops.

Appreciate the hold.

Best,
